KEY MESSAGE 1...- Elevated heat and humidity continues through the weekend. 
Scattered showers and thunderstorms possible tonight and Saturday 
afternoon & evening. 

Day Cloud Phase satellite imagery shows development of diurnal 
cumulus across portions of southern New England this afternoon. 
SHowers and thunderstorms continue to develop across PA and NY along 
the periphery of a mid-level ridge shifted offshore of southern New 
England. For the rest of the afternoon, expect mainly dry 
conditions. With a few cells beginning to pop near southern NY, 
can't rule out an isolated thunderstorm in western MA/CT after 4 PM. 
Daytime heating has allowed instability values to rise into marginal 
ranges this afternoon to support pop-up showers/storms. An 
isolated shower or storm may possibly initiate of the sea breeze
boundary along the south coast as well late this afternoon. Hi-
res guidance continues to bring a more consistent batch of 
remnant scattered showers and a few storms after 8 PM tonight. 
The best chance for seeing a storm will be in western southern 
New England. With precipitable water values approaching 2 
inches, brief heavy downpours are possible. This batch of 
showers/storms are likely to weaken and diminish as they push 
east overnight. With increased cloud cover for much of the 
overnight and the warm airmass, overnight temperatures likely 
remain in the upper 60s and low 70s tonight. 

Saturday, the mid-level ridge pushes further southeast of the region 
with flow becoming more zonal. The warm/moist airmass will stay in 
place tomorrow with SW flow supplying advection of higher dewpoints 
in the low 70s. Expect another day of elevated humidity and 
slightly above normal temperatures in the mid to upper 80s. With
the added humidity it may feel closer to low to mid 90s. There 
still is potential for scattered showers and thunderstorms in 
the late afternoon/evening on Saturday. Model guidance indicated
a weak embedded disturbance moving through the flow which 
should help provide additional support for thunderstorms 
accompanied by the diurnal heating and moist/unstable airmass. 
However, there the CAMs continue to show a spread in solutions 
with regards to potential and location across southern New 
England. Some solutions indicate more isolated potential, 
keeping the higher activity south of the region. Others are more
robust, simulating a few clusters of thunderstorms pushing 
across southern New England Sat evening. The primary concern 
with any storms will be localized heavy downpours supported by 
PWATs approaching 1.8". Mid- level flow is sufficient to keep 
storms moving from west to east which minimizes the concern for 
more widespread flash flooding issues. Can't rule out localized 
flash flooding if a storm or two were to push over a more 
vulnerable area (urban/poor drainage, area of recent heavy 
rainfall). 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Summer warmth and humidity continues along with a daily
chance of a pop-up shower or thunderstorm.

There haven't been many notable changes to the extended portion of 
the forecast, which encompasses Sunday through the upcoming week. In 
general, this timeframe features continued summer warmth with 
manageable humidity and daily chances for afternoon showers or 
thunderstorms. As mentioned previously, the synoptic pattern trends 
toward a flattening mid-level ridge, with nearly zonal flow across 
the CONUS and the subtropical ridge expanding from the western 
Atlantic into the lower third of the CONUS. This will allow westerly 
flow with embedded shortwave disturbances to move through the region.

Temperatures aloft remain quite warm, with 925mb temperatures around 
+23C to +25C from Sunday through Tuesday. BUFKIT forecast soundings 
depict a well-mixed boundary layer, supporting afternoon 
temperatures well into the upper 80s to around 90F. Dew points will 
remain elevated, though should fall short of oppressive levels, 
generally in the 65F to 70F range. Nevertheless, this will 
contribute to heat indices in the lower 90s Sunday through Tuesday. 
A potential break from the summer warmth arrives during the middle 
portion of next week as a front moves through, though there remains 
a fair amount of spread among the guidance regarding the exact 
evolution of this feature. Given the uncertainty, stayed close to 
NBM guidance for Wednesday and beyond, with highs expected to be in 
the lower to middle 80s. Overnight temperatures will remain 
seasonably warm, with lows generally in the 60s.

Regarding thunderstorm chances, embedded shortwave disturbances 
moving through the zonal flow should provide sufficient lift for 
isolated to scattered thunderstorms each day. Storms should remain 
largely pulse-type and disorganized rather than evolving into 
organized severe convection. PWATs up to around 2.0 inches will 
further support the potential for localized downpours. Gusty winds 
and frequent lightning will be the primary hazards. That said,
